main_text.p: vium non patiens) ullus daretur : & tamen vadando alios ad pectus usque undis immersos, alios natando, utrosque toto corpore nudos, tædas vero sine flammis ferentes, ne conspici e longinquo possent, per noctis tenebras, qua hostium nemo expectaverat, illuc devenisse, & accensis repente tædis, summa audacia non vulnera non mortem veritos, per medios hostes armatos & resistentes ad machinas velut lymphatas sese intulisse, easque incendio dedisse, quinetiam hostes tanta audacia perculsos in fugam compulisse & eorum castra terrore complevisse, ac tandem re, ob quam venerant, patrata, eadem via, qua venerant, & eodem modo ad suos revertisse: Scipionem ægre fugam suorum sistere, & trepida-tionem comprimere potuisse : verum tamen sedata consternatione loeum[?] illum recuperasse, operibusq; munivissete.[?], impositisque ei quatuor armatorum millibus & machinis novis constructisps[?] proxima urbis inde infesta habuisse. acta hæc vergente jam æstate. page.notes: The scan shows a faint, mirrored column of marks along the left edge; this is show-through or the edge of the neighbouring page and is left out. Right-margin marks are small and partly illegible; the readings "te.", "ps" and "scr." are doubtful. "loeum" is doubtful as printed. The word "Scipio" / "nem" at the line end is not clearly hyphenated on the scan. The text ends on a half word, "ce-", with the catchword "pisse" at the foot.
